items.title: Foreign Minister Khanal begins bilateral meetings in New York
items.blurb: Foreign leaders and senior officials voice solidarity over Nepal’s climate justice position and flood recovery on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

items.title: Balendra Shah’s UN appearance draws diplomatic interest in New York
items.blurb: Nepal’s prime minister is set to address the General Assembly on climate justice, the Bhotekoshi floods and the concerns of mountain countries.

items.title: What the Bhotekoshi flood revealed about Nepal’s health system
items.blurb: The emergency phase of the flood has largely been contained, but the most demanding work still lies ahead.

items.title: New hybrid maize variety ‘Saugat’ promises relief for farmers facing extreme weather
items.blurb: The variety is on the verge of official certification and release after nearly 11 years of rigorous multi-stage field trials and continuous testing.

items.title: The nurse who wanted to heal Rasuwa
items.blurb: Pratima Tamang Lama was a nurse, community worker, and ambitious local leader who dreamed of becoming Nepal’s health minister. The Bhotekoshi flood cut those dreams short.

items.title: Nepal unlikely to hold donor conference for reconstruction
items.blurb: The government plans to seek funds through bilateral negotiations with major donors.

items.title: Swarnim Wagle calls for a reset in Nepal-India ties, says era of anti-India nationalism is over
items.blurb: In an interview with The Hindu, the finance minister says Kathmandu wants to focus on trade, connectivity, energy, and reconstruction while constructively addressing contentious issues such as the boundary dispute.

items.title: AfD leads as Merz rues ‘disaster’ in worst state election result in postwar Germany
items.blurb: The AfD’s strong showing in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and gains in Berlin deepen pressure on Merz as his coalition faces voter anger over economic reforms and rising living costs.

items.title: Welcome to a terrifying new climate era
items.blurb: The Bhotekoshi crisis must be recognised as a clear signal that we have entered a new era in our rapidly warming world.
